subject: Post-call: CareLoop feature pricing sensitivity + payback next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Sharma <amit@careloop.com>, Priya Rao <priya@careloop.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 14:03:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + quick note on $/1M token targets and next steps

Hi Amit / Priya — thanks for the time earlier today. Quick recap and the pieces we promised to surface so you can validate internally. I copied Priyom (AE) and Monica (CS) so we have alignment on pricing and PoC scope.

Top-line from the call (notes attached):
- Primary use case: "Smart Summaries" (user-facing summary of care notes + visit transcripts).
- Expected usage profile (your estimates): 2.5k DAU initial, rising to 10k over 12 months.
- Calls per user: 1.5 average / day during peak flows (batching possible for background jobs).
- Median prompt + response size: ~700 tokens; 95th percentile ~2,800 tokens.
- Baseline monthly token scenarios we discussed: conservative ~15M/mo, expected ~45M/mo, upside ~150M/mo.

Budget & unit-econ signals you shared:
- Procurement/budget target for inference + infra: $10k–15k / month for the initial product line (first 6–9 months).
- Procurement prefers a target run-rate unit cost near: $/1M tokens in the range of $40–$70 (your internal goal is to keep inference spend comfortably under $/feature contribution targets).

Initial Redwood cost assumptions (back-of-envelope) — please treat as placeholders until we run PoC telemetry:
- Hosted rate (no commit): $90 per 1M tokens (estimate for the current model family at default perf).
- Negotiated reserved / committed profile: target $/1M tokens ≈ $40–$60 depending on commit and quantization profile.
- With your conservative scenario (15M/mo) at $60 per 1M tokens -> monthly inference cost ≈ $900. At expected (45M/mo) -> ≈ $2,700.

Questions / asks for us to firm an initial commercial proposal:
1) Confirm which scenario is most defensible for procurement (15/45/150M).
2) Share a simple conversion/revenue model: ARPA per user and target gross margin for the feature (we started discussing $5 ARPA and a 65–75% gross margin target).
3) Any non-negotiable SLOs (p95 latency target, retention/PKI constraints) that will affect hosting choice.

Next proposed steps (short timeline):
- Internal calc & proposal (this week): Priyom will produce an SOW + price options (hosted vs reserved) and a 6-week PoC estimate.
- PoC kickoff: target week of Dec 6th if procurement OKs quick NDAs + PO for PoC credits.
- Technical kickoff: Monica will lead instrumentation and eval suite for quality regressions.

Attachments: careloop-discovery-notes.pdf (call notes), careloop-token-estimates.xlsx (token scenarios).

Thanks — I will follow up with a short note that includes the 3 commercial scenarios (hosted, 6-mo reserved, 12-mo reserved) and an initial CAC/payback sketch.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Amit Sharma <amit@careloop.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@careloop.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick note on $/1M token targets and next steps

Thanks Tessa — useful summary. A couple of clarifications from our side:
- Budget band ($10k–15k / mo) is the procurement guideline for the feature family (Smart Summaries + 2 related UX features). We can reallocate if we see clear ROI from a PoC.
- The $/1M target we threw out is aspirational; procurement prefers a committed/unit-based number they can forecast against.

A few asks:
1) Can you sketch a PoC cost for the conservative and expected scenarios (15M and 45M) that includes both inference runtime and a small buffer for canary/rollouts?
2) Can you highlight what changes if we want <300ms p95 for 700-token responses (this was raised as a preferred SLO by our product lead)?

We are ready to move on NDA and PoC once we have a ballpark commercial footprint to present to procurement on Monday.

—Amit
Head of Product, CareLoop
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Internal — quick PoC & unit-econ sketches for CareLoop

Folks — I ran the quick numbers off Tessa's notes. High-level assumptions and suggested commercial scenarios attached (poC-cost-outline.pdf). Summary below: 

Assumptions (conservative):
- Baseline tokens: 15M / month.
- Avg tokens per call: 700.
- Calls/day implied: ~714 calls/day overall (conservative active user mix).

Scenarios (monthly inference spend, rounded):
1) Hosted (no commit): 15M @ $90/1M -> $1,350 / month. 45M -> $4,050 / month.
2) 6-month reserved (mid-commit): estimated $55/1M -> 15M -> $825 / month; 45M -> $2,475 / month.
3) 12-month reserved (high commit): estimated $42/1M -> 15M -> $630 / month; 45M -> $1,890 / month.

Feature-level unit economics (example using your ARPA signal):
- ARPA (Smart Summaries): $5 / user / month (you mentioned this).
- Paying users initial: 2,500 -> MRR = $12,500.
- Gross margin target for product: 70% -> contribution margin = $3.50 / user / month -> contribution = $8,750 / month.
- If inference cost (reserved 6-mo) at 15M = $825, that leaves ~ $7.9k / month to cover other infra, support, and contribution.

CAC/payback calculus (simple):
- Target payback = 6 months -> allowable CAC per new user = ARPA * payback * margin = $5 * 6 * 0.70 = $21.
- For a 2,500-user base expansion, total CAC budget = $52.5k.

Ask / risk flags to surface to CareLoop:
- Latency SLO <300ms p95 will push us toward reserved capacity and possibly model family selection (lower precision / quantized models to hit price/latency). That materially affects $/1M numbers — I'll mark that in the PoC outline.
- Token distribution tail (95th percentile spikes) will increase cost by ~12–18% unless we implement prefix caching or aggressive truncation.

Next internal steps:
- Draft SOW + 3 commercial options (hosted, 6m res, 12m res) — ready EOD Mon.
- Engineering to confirm latency feasibility for <300ms p95 on recommended model family. Rishi, can you validate perf matrix?

Priyom
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Sharma <amit@careloop.com>, Priya Rao <priya@careloop.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + quick note on $/1M token targets and next steps

Amit / Priya — thanks for the quick reply. Priyom and I attached a concise PoC cost outline (poC-cost-outline.pdf) that shows the 3 scenarios we discussed (hosted / 6m reserved / 12m reserved) with the cost math in the second tab of the workbook. Highlighting the short answer here:

- For your procurement band ($10k–15k/mo), the expected baseline (15M) fits easily within margin if you target a 6–12 month reserved commitment (estimated $42–$55 / 1M tokens).
- If you want <300ms p95 for 700-token responses we will need a reserved footprint and smaller model family; that increases engineering lift and modifies the price toward the higher end of the reserved estimates while giving latency guarantees.

Proposed next steps to get procurement comfortable:
1) We can run a 6-week PoC with usage capped to mirror your conservative scenario (15M cap). Estimated PoC runtime inference spend (hosted run for telemetry + a small reserved buffer) is $1,200–$2,000 — Redwood covers up to $1,000 in credits; balance billed to CareLoop PO.
2) If PoC demonstrates the expected latency/quality, we will present a reserved offer (6- or 12-month) with explicit $/1M token tiers and a migration plan.

If that works, I will: (a) send NDA + PoC SOW for signature, (b) schedule technical kickoff with Monica and your engineering lead for Dec 7th.

Would you prefer we show the math as $/1M tokens or per-feature cost per 1,000 active users? Happy to do both; I put both in the attached workbook.

Best regards,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
